name: ZeroCloud Seek
description: Find your nearby devices. Follow the signal, then ring them.
introduction: Seek is being designed to help you find a misplaced phone, tablet or computer using your trusted devices. Start with nearby signals, then let a sound guide you the rest of the way.

steps.title: Add your devices
steps.description: Pair the devices you trust before you need to find them.

steps.title: Follow the signal
steps.description: Use Bluetooth and local connections for proximity clues. More precise ranging would depend on compatible hardware.

steps.title: Make it ring
steps.description: Ask a reachable device to play a sound. Flash and vibration are also planned where the device allows them.

note.title: Your devices. Your search.
note.description: Trusted pairing, encrypted communication and explicit permission to find or ring a device are core requirements. Your device list and last-seen history should stay under your control, with no required cloud account.

faqs.question: How would Seek find a device?
faqs.answer: Seek is planned to combine Bluetooth discovery, local-network reachability and signal trends. Signal strength can suggest whether you are getting closer; it cannot reliably give an exact distance or direction. Supported technologies such as UWB or Wi-Fi RTT could improve ranging on compatible devices.

faqs.question: Could Seek show a map?
faqs.answer: An estimated search area is part of the plan. Placing it on a map needs a reference, such as known device positions or a calibrated floor plan, plus suitable measurements. Radio-based room mapping is a research direction, not a promise that any phone can scan walls or reconstruct every room.

faqs.question: Would it work without the internet?
faqs.answer: Local finding is the goal. Previously paired devices should be able to cooperate over supported nearby connections without a cloud service. Radio range, device permissions and background restrictions still apply.

faqs.question: What if the device is offline or switched off?
faqs.answer: Live finding and ringing need a reachable, powered device. When it cannot be reached, Seek is planned to show locally saved last-seen information, including its age. That is a historical clue, not a current location. Other trusted devices could contribute sightings when they can detect it.

faqs.question: Could it ring a muted device?
faqs.answer: Ringing, flashing and vibration will depend on what each platform permits. Seek cannot promise to override silent mode, system restrictions or a device that has lost power.

faqs.question: Who could find or ring my devices?
faqs.answer: Only devices and people you explicitly authorize should be able to request a search or a ring. Secure enrollment, authenticated commands and encrypted connections are required parts of the design. Seek is not intended to track arbitrary nearby devices or people.

faqs.question: Will there be a Web version?
faqs.answer: A Web companion is planned, with a placeholder in Downloads. Browser radio access and background operation are limited, so some finding features may require the native app. There is no public build or web app yet.
